Methodology & sources

What this dashboard is

A business-development prospecting tool for professional-services practices — the analogue of the physician BD dashboard, extended to law, accounting/CPA, architecture & engineering, IT & management consulting, and other professional firms (NAICS sector 54). It answers two questions: which specific firms are warm, financeable prospects right now, and how big is the total market those prospects sit inside.

Data sources

  • SBA 7(a) & 504 FOIA borrowers — the in-repo loan-maturity/loans.json, the public SBA loan-approval disclosure already footprint-filtered to the Texas target counties. Filtered here to NAICS sector 54 and tagged with a human subsector label from the 4-digit code. Each row is a real firm with a known financing relationship — the definition of a warm lead.
  • BLS QCEW (Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages) — the near-census of establishments and employment covered by unemployment insurance. Pulled live from the QCEW Open Data CSV slices (data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/{year}/a/area/{fips}.csv), private ownership (own_code=5), county × 4-digit NAICS (agglvl=76). Provides the total addressable market — establishments and employment per subsector per county — for the statewide footprint (all 254 Texas counties). Free, no key.

Prospect score (0–100)

  • Loan size (0–30) — square-root scale, full credit at $2M+. Bigger existing facilities signal bigger practices and bigger opportunities.
  • Recency (0–25) — linear decay over 72 months from approval; a recent approval is a live, engaged borrower.
  • Above-market rate (0–25) — how far the loan's rate sits above the median 54xx rate (the refinance / win-back upside), with a bonus for variable-rate loans that are easiest to reprice.
  • Active status (0–20) — current & committed loans score highest; distressed less; paid-off / cancelled firms retain a small score as proven borrowers worth re-engaging.

Subsector buckets

Legal (5411) · Accounting & Tax (5412) · Arch-Eng (architecture 5413 + specialized design 5414) · Consulting (computer systems design 5415 + management consulting 5416) · Other (scientific R&D 5417 + advertising 5418 + other professional 5419).

Limitations

  • SBA shows only firms with SBA financing — not all professional practices. Cash-financed firms, bank-conventional borrowers and unlevered practices never appear. The prospect list is a warm subset, not a census.
  • QCEW gives market totals, not names. There is no public individual-firm registry for these professions the way there is an NPI file for physicians, so the market-sizing side is counts and employment only — it cannot be joined to specific firms.
  • QCEW is annual and lags; county × subsector cells may be suppressed for disclosure in the smallest markets and then read as zero.
  • Loan amounts are original approval amounts, not current balances; the score is a prospecting heuristic, not a credit decision.

Refresh: python professional-services/refresh.py — reads the in-repo SBA file and auto-detects the latest QCEW annual year.
